cohort: The study included 18 patients with endometrial cancer (cases) and 19 patients undergoing surgery for pelvic organ prolapse or uterine fibroids without neoplastic lesions (control group).
finding: The study found an increased expression of miR-205-5p in endometrial cancer tissue and decreased expression of miR-222-3p in both tissue and serum samples, suggesting miR-205-5p and miR-222-3p as potential endometrial cancer biomarkers, with miR-222-3p being a potential easily accessible serum marker.
cross-section timing: At the time of surgery/sample collection.
